note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 65; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 17) on data/benches/buffer.json: a buffer made and its capacity. Henderson and Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log10(n(A-) / n(HA)), 4.76 for acetic acid; a buffer holds its pH because an acid added turns its acetate into acetic acid, which is weak.
title: Experiment: a buffer and its capacity

report.label: the buffer's pH
report.why: Henderson and Hasselbalch give 4.76 + log10(n(acetate) / n(acid)): the balance's reading over 82.03 g/mol, against the pipette's 25 mL of 0.40 M. The pH meter reads a little lower, about 4.65: it reads the hydrogen ion's activity, and in a solution of 0.1 M of ions their activity is about four fifths of their concentration.

report.label: the buffer's pH after the acid
report.why: 0.2 mmol of acid turns 0.2 mmol of the 2.5 mmol of acetate in 25 mL into acetic acid: log10(2.3 / 2.7) moves the pH by only 0.07.

report.label: the water's pH after the acid
report.why: In water nothing takes the acid's hydrogen ions: 0.2 mmol in 27 mL is 0.0074 M, pH 2.1, from 7.

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: You will make 100 mL holding 10 mmol of acetic acid and 10 mmol of its salt, sodium acetate. What pH do you expect? Henderson and Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log10(acetate / acid), acetic acid's pKa 4.76. Type it, then click "predict".

steps.title: The flask on the balance
steps.text: Click the volumetric flask to pick it up, then click the balance. Then right-click the balance and click "tare".

checks.text: the flask tared on the balance

steps.title: About 0.82 g of sodium acetate
steps.text: Pick up the sodium acetate, right-click the flask, type 0.82 and click "tip 0.82 g of the solid". Then right-click the balance and click "+ mass".
steps.why: Sodium acetate, CH3COONa, is 82.03 g/mol: 0.82 g is 10 mmol.

steps.title: 25 mL of the acid
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click the acetic acid: it draws to its mark. Then pick it up again and click the volumetric flask.
steps.why: 25 mL of 0.40 M acetic acid is 10 mmol.

steps.title: Until it is empty
steps.text: Wait until the pipette has run out.

steps.title: To the mark, and mixed
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click a free square. Pick up the water bottle, right-click the flask and click "to the mark". Then right-click the flask, click "stir", and click 60x on the clock.

steps.title: Its pH
steps.text: Click 1x on the clock. Right-click the flask and click "+ pH": the buffer's pH, against what you predicted.

steps.title: 25 mL of it, and 25 mL of water
steps.text: Pick up the volumetric flask, right-click beaker A, type 25 and click "pour". Then pick up the water bottle, right-click beaker B, type 25 and click "pour".

steps.title: Their pH
steps.text: Right-click beaker A and click "+ pH"; then beaker B.

steps.title: The same acid into each
steps.text: Pick up the hydrochloric acid, right-click beaker A, type 2 and click "pour"; then the same into beaker B. Stir each: right-click it and click "stir". Then click 60x.
steps.why: 2 mL of 0.100 M is 0.2 mmol of hydrogen ions into each.

steps.title: Their pH again
steps.text: Click 1x. Right-click beaker A and click "+ pH"; then beaker B. The buffer barely moved; the water fell from 7 to about 2.
